# url - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/url/^2.5/

## Expand description

rust-url is an implementation of the [URL Standard](http://url.spec.whatwg.org/)
for the [Rust](http://rust-lang.org/) programming language.

[§](https://docs.rs#url-parsing-and-data-structures)URL parsing and data structures

First, URL parsing may fail for various reasons and therefore returns a `Result`.

```
use url::{Url, ParseError};
assert!(Url::parse("http://[:::1]") == Err(ParseError::InvalidIpv6Address))
```
Let’s parse a valid URL and look at its components.

```
use url::{Url, Host, Position};
let issue_list_url = Url::parse(
    "https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues?labels=E-easy&state=open"
)?;
assert!(issue_list_url.scheme() == "https");
assert!(issue_list_url.username() == "");
assert!(issue_list_url.password() == None);
assert!(issue_list_url.host_str() == Some("github.com"));
assert!(issue_list_url.host() == Some(Host::Domain("github.com")));
assert!(issue_list_url.port() == None);
assert!(issue_list_url.path() == "/rust-lang/rust/issues");
assert!(issue_list_url.path_segments().map(|c| c.collect::<Vec<_>>()) ==
        Some(vec!["rust-lang", "rust", "issues"]));
assert!(issue_list_url.query() == Some("labels=E-easy&state=open"));
assert!(&issue_list_url[Position::BeforePath..] == "/rust-lang/rust/issues?labels=E-easy&state=open");
assert!(issue_list_url.fragment() == None);
assert!(!issue_list_url.cannot_be_a_base());
```
Some URLs are said to be *cannot-be-a-base*:
they don’t have a username, password, host, or port,
and their “path” is an arbitrary string rather than slash-separated segments:

```
use url::Url;
let data_url = Url::parse("data:text/plain,Hello?World#")?;
assert!(data_url.cannot_be_a_base());
assert!(data_url.scheme() == "data");
assert!(data_url.path() == "text/plain,Hello");
assert!(data_url.path_segments().is_none());
assert!(data_url.query() == Some("World"));
assert!(data_url.fragment() == Some(""));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#default-features)Default Features

Versions `<= 2.5.2` of the crate have no default features. Versions `> 2.5.2` have the default feature ‘std’.
If you are upgrading across this boundary and you have specified `default-features = false`, then
you will need to add the ‘std’ feature or the ‘alloc’ feature to your dependency.
The ‘std’ feature has the same behavior as the previous versions. The ‘alloc’ feature
provides no_std support.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Enable the `serde` feature to include `Deserialize` and `Serialize` implementations for `url::Url`.

[§](https://docs.rs#base-url)Base URL

Many contexts allow URL *references* that can be relative to a *base URL*:

`<link rel="stylesheet" href="../main.css">`Since parsed URLs are absolute, giving a base is required for parsing relative URLs:

```
use url::{Url, ParseError};
assert!(Url::parse("../main.css") == Err(ParseError::RelativeUrlWithoutBase))
```
Use the `join` method on an `Url` to use it as a base URL:

```
use url::Url;
let this_document = Url::parse("http://servo.github.io/rust-url/url/index.html")?;
let css_url = this_document.join("../main.css")?;
assert_eq!(css_url.as_str(), "http://servo.github.io/rust-url/main.css");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-serde)Feature: `serde`

If you enable the `serde` feature, [ Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html) will implement

[and](https://docs.rs/serde/1/serde/trait.Serialize.html)

`serde::Serialize`[. See](https://docs.rs/serde/1/serde/trait.Deserialize.html)

`serde::Deserialize`[serde documentation](https://serde.rs)for more information.

`url = { version = "2", features = ["serde"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-debugger_visualizer)Feature: `debugger_visualizer`

If you enable the `debugger_visualizer` feature, the `url` crate will include
a [natvis file](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/debugger/create-custom-views-of-native-objects)
for [Visual Studio](https://www.visualstudio.com/) that allows you to view
[ Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html) objects in the debugger.

This feature requires Rust 1.71 or later.

`url = { version = "2", features = ["debugger_visualizer"] }`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [form_urlencoded](https://docs.rs/form_urlencoded/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/form_urlencoded/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Opaque](https://docs.rs/struct.OpaqueOrigin.html)- Origin
- Opaque identifier for URLs that have file or other schemes
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseOptions.html)- Options
- Full configuration for the URL parser.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.PathSegmentsMut.html)- Segments - Mut
- Exposes methods to manipulate the path of an URL that is not cannot-be-base.
- [Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html)
- A parsed URL record.
- [UrlQuery](https://docs.rs/struct.UrlQuery.html)
- Implementation detail of `Url::query_pairs_mut`. Typically not used directly.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.Host.html)
- The host name of an URL.
- [Origin](https://docs.rs/enum.Origin.html)
- The origin of an URL
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- Errors that can occur during parsing.
- [Position](https://docs.rs/enum.Position.html)
- Indicates a position within a URL based on its components.
- [Syntax](https://docs.rs/enum.SyntaxViolation.html)- Violation
- Non-fatal syntax violations that can occur during parsing.

# num_rational - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/num-rational/^0.4/

## Expand description

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseRatioError.html)- Ratio - Error
- [Ratio](https://docs.rs/struct.Ratio.html)
- Represents the ratio between two numbers.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [BigRational](https://docs.rs/type.BigRational.html)
- Alias for arbitrary precision rationals.
- [Rational](https://docs.rs/type.Rational.html)- Deprecated
- Alias for a `Ratio`of machine-sized integers.
- [Rational32](https://docs.rs/type.Rational32.html)
- Alias for a `Ratio`of 32-bit-sized integers.
- [Rational64](https://docs.rs/type.Rational64.html)
- Alias for a `Ratio`of 64-bit-sized integers.

# sim_kernel - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

sim-kernel is the small protocol kernel of the SIM Rust runtime.

The kernel defines contracts; libraries supply behavior. This crate holds
the protocol and contract types – forms, values, stores, registry and
callable surfaces, the [ shape](https://docs.rs/shape/index.html) protocol, evaluation policy, and the ABI
transport – while concrete behavior (parsers, number domains, the standard
distribution, and server/agent/browse implementations) lives in separate
library crates loaded against these contracts. SIM is a Rust runtime, not a
Lisp runtime; Lisp is one codec surface among several.

The one deliberate exception is the pair of built-in *reference backends*:
[ list::VecList](https://docs.rs/list/struct.VecList.html) (a

[) and](https://docs.rs/list/trait.ListValue.html)

`list::ListValue`[(a](https://docs.rs/table/struct.AssocTable.html)

`table::AssocTable`[). These are the kernel’s bootstrap list and table implementations – minimal, correct, and self-annotated](https://docs.rs/table/trait.Table.html)

`table::Table``sim-non-citizen` –
so the runtime can stand up collections before any library loads. They are
reference implementations, not the only backends: alternatives load as libs
against the [/](https://docs.rs/list/trait.ListBackend.html)

`list::ListBackend`[contracts. (Future cleanup: move even these into a default-loaded distribution lib so the kernel ships pure contracts; tracked against the constellation reorg.)](https://docs.rs/table/trait.TableBackend.html)

`table::TableBackend`The kernel data flow is:

`tokens -> checked forms -> objects -> checked calls -> objects -> encoded forms`[§](https://docs.rs#module-map)Module map

Core forms and values: [ value](https://docs.rs/value/index.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/expr/index.html)

`expr`[,](https://docs.rs/term/index.html)

`term`[,](https://docs.rs/encode/index.html)

`encode`[,](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)

`error`[,](https://docs.rs/id/index.html)

`id`[.](https://docs.rs/ref_id/index.html)

`ref_id`Data substrate: [ datum](https://docs.rs/datum/index.html),

# sim_lib_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-core/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Shared surface-pack substrate for SIM runtime libraries.

The kernel defines the `Lib`/`Registry`/`ExportRecord` contracts; this crate
supplies the shared substrate for declaring exported value cards as data and
installing them once, idempotently, into a registry.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use surface::`- [SurfaceField](https://docs.rs/surface/enum.SurfaceField.html);
- `pub use surface::`- [SurfacePackLib](https://docs.rs/surface/struct.SurfacePackLib.html);
- `pub use surface::`- [SurfacePackSpec](https://docs.rs/surface/struct.SurfacePackSpec.html);
- `pub use surface::`- [SurfaceValueSpec](https://docs.rs/surface/struct.SurfaceValueSpec.html);
- `pub use surface::`- [card_expr](https://docs.rs/surface/fn.card_expr.html);
- `pub use surface::`- [install_once](https://docs.rs/surface/fn.install_once.html);
- `pub use surface::`- [install_once_id](https://docs.rs/surface/fn.install_once_id.html);
- `pub use surface::`- [installed_lib_id](https://docs.rs/surface/fn.installed_lib_id.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [surface](https://docs.rs/surface/index.html)
- Surface-pack card libs and idempotent install.

## Statics[§](https://docs.rs#statics)

- [RECIPES](https://docs.rs/static.RECIPES.html)
- Recipes embedded at build time from this crate’s `recipes/`tree.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [manifest_](https://docs.rs/fn.manifest_name.html)- name
- Returns the manifest name under which this surface pack installs (`lisp:core`).

# sim_lib_midi_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-midi-core/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Core MIDI data model and in-memory I/O for the SIM music stack.

This crate defines the protocol-agnostic MIDI types shared across the
constellation: tick-based timing ([ TickTime](https://docs.rs/struct.TickTime.html)), the bounded integer
domains used by MIDI bytes (

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.U7.html)

`U7`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.U14.html)

`U14`[), the event model (](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html)

`Channel`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiEvent.html)

`MidiEvent`[,](https://docs.rs/enum.MidiPayload.html)

`MidiPayload`[,](https://docs.rs/enum.ChannelMessage.html)

`ChannelMessage`[,](https://docs.rs/enum.MetaEvent.html)

`MetaEvent`[), and the streaming](https://docs.rs/enum.SysExEvent.html)

`SysExEvent`[/](https://docs.rs/trait.MidiSource.html)

`MidiSource`[traits with in-memory implementations. It also provides the](https://docs.rs/trait.MidiSink.html)

`MidiSink`[transform, controller-number constants, tempo conversions, and the host-registered](https://docs.rs/struct.NoteEchoPlayer.html)

`NoteEchoPlayer`[that exposes the in-memory cards to a running SIM](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiIoLib.html)

`MidiIoLib`[.](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/env/core/struct.Cx.html)

`Cx`Higher layers (Standard MIDI File, SysEx, live transports) build on this model rather than redefining it.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sim_lib_midi_core::{Channel, ChannelMessage, U7};
let note = ChannelMessage::NoteOn {
    ch: Channel::new(0).unwrap(),
    key: U7(60),
    vel: U7(100),
};
assert!(matches!(note, ChannelMessage::NoteOn { .. }));
```
```
use sim_lib_midi_core::TickTime;
// 480 ticks at 480 tpq is exactly one quarter note.
let one_quarter = TickTime::new(480, 480).unwrap();
assert_eq!(one_quarter.as_f64_quarters(), 1.0);
// Rebasing to a coarser resolution is exact here.
assert_eq!(one_quarter.rebase(96).unwrap().ticks, 96);
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [meta_](https://docs.rs/meta_view/index.html)- view
- Typed views over raw `MetaBucket`
- [wire](https://docs.rs/wire/index.html)
- Canonical MIDI channel-message wire bytes.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Channel](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html)
- A MIDI channel number in the range `0..=15`.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryMidiSink.html)- Midi - Sink
- An in-memory `MidiSink`
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryMidiSource.html)- Midi - Source
- An in-memory `MidiSource`
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryTrackedMidiSource.html)- Tracked - Midi - Source
- An in-memory `TrackedMidiSource`
- [Meta](https://docs.rs/struct.MetaBucket.html)- Bucket
- A raw meta event: its type byte plus payload bytes.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiEvent.html)- Event
- A timestamped MIDI event with provenance.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiIoLib.html)- IoLib
- Host-registered lib exporting the in-memory MIDI I/O cards and registry,
built on the shared `SurfacePackLib`
- [Note](https://docs.rs/struct.NoteEchoConfig.html)- Echo - Config
- Configuration for the `NoteEchoPlayer`
- [Note](https://docs.rs/struct.NoteEchoPlayer.html)- Echo - Player
- Renders rhythmic note echoes from an input event stream per a
`NoteEchoConfig`
- [Note](https://docs.rs/struct.NoteEchoRender.html)- Echo - Render
- The result of a `NoteEchoPlayer`
- [Note](https://docs.rs/struct.NoteEchoTrace.html)- Echo - Trace
- A record of a single emitted echo, linking it back to its source note.
- [RawBytes](https://docs.rs/struct.RawBytes.html)
- An uninterpreted run of bytes with a status byte, used as a fallback.
- [Smpte](https://docs.rs/struct.SmpteOffset.html)- Offset
- An SMPTE timecode offset, as carried by the SMPTE-offset meta event.
- [Tick](https://docs.rs/struct.TickTime.html)- Time
- A point in musical time measured in ticks at a given resolution.
- [Tracked](https://docs.rs/struct.TrackedMidiEvent.html)- Midi - Event
- A `MidiEvent`
- [U7](https://docs.rs/struct.U7.html)
- A 7-bit MIDI data value in the range `0..=127`.
- [U14](https://docs.rs/struct.U14.html)
- A 14-bit MIDI data value in the range `0..=16_383`, as used by pitch bend.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Channel](https://docs.rs/enum.ChannelMessage.html)- Message
- A MIDI channel-voice message, carrying its target `Channel`
- [Meta](https://docs.rs/enum.MetaEvent.html)- Event
- A meta event: track-scoped information that is not transmitted over the
wire, recognised types plus an `Other`
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/enum.MidiError.html)- Error
- Errors produced when constructing or converting core MIDI values.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/enum.MidiPayload.html)- Payload
- The payload of a `MidiEvent`
- [Note](https://docs.rs/enum.NoteEchoChannelPolicy.html)- Echo - Channel - Policy
- Controls which channel each echoed note is emitted on.
- [Note](https://docs.rs/enum.NoteEchoScaleSnap.html)- Echo - Scale - Snap
- Controls whether echoed notes are snapped to a scale.
- [Pump](https://docs.rs/enum.PumpError.html)- Error
- An error raised while pumping events from a source into a sink, recording which side failed.
- [SysEx](https://docs.rs/enum.SysExEvent.html)- Event
- A system-exclusive event, distinguished by its leading status byte.

- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_FOOT_MSB.html)- FOOT_ - MSB
- Foot Controller (MSB), controller 4.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_LOCAL_CONTROL.html)- LOCAL_ - CONTROL
- Local Control On/Off (channel mode), controller 122.

- Modulation Wheel (MSB), controller 1.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_PAN_MSB.html)- PAN_ - MSB
- Pan (MSB), controller 10.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_PORTAMENTO_SWITCH.html)- PORTAMENTO_ - SWITCH
- Portamento On/Off switch, controller 65.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_PORTAMENTO_TIME_MSB.html)- PORTAMENTO_ - TIME_ - MSB
- Portamento Time (MSB), controller 5.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_RESET_ALL_CONTROLLERS.html)- RESET_ - ALL_ - CONTROLLERS
- Reset All Controllers (channel mode), controller 121.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_SOFT_PEDAL.html)- SOFT_ - PEDAL
- Soft Pedal, controller 67.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_SOSTENUTO.html)- SOSTENUTO
- Sostenuto Pedal, controller 66.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_SUSTAIN_PEDAL.html)- SUSTAIN_ - PEDAL
- Sustain (damper) Pedal, controller 64.
- [CC_](https://docs.rs/constant.CC_VOLUME_MSB.html)- VOLUME_ - MSB
- Channel Volume (MSB), controller 7.
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_US_PER_QUARTER.html)- US_ - PER_ - QUARTER
- The default MIDI tempo of 500_000 microseconds per quarter (120 BPM).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [bpm_](https://docs.rs/fn.bpm_to_us_per_quarter.html)- to_ - us_ - per_ - quarter
- Converts beats per minute to microseconds per quarter note (rounded).
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_midi_io_lib.html)- midi_ - io_ - lib
- Installs `MidiIoLib``cx`once and registers the in-memory source, sink, and tracked-source export records.
- [pump](https://docs.rs/fn.pump.html)
- Drains every event from `source`into`sink`, re-timing events to the sink’s resolution, and returns the number of events transferred.
- [stable_](https://docs.rs/fn.stable_midi_event_order.html)- midi_ - event_ - order
- Sorts events into a stable, deterministic order by time and then by a payload tiebreak (note-offs before note-ons at the same tick).
- [synthetic_](https://docs.rs/fn.synthetic_origin.html)- origin
- Returns an `Origin`
- [us_](https://docs.rs/fn.us_per_quarter_to_bpm.html)- per_ - quarter_ - to_ - bpm
- Converts microseconds per quarter note to beats per minute.

# sim_lib_midi_smf - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-midi-smf/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Standard MIDI File (SMF) reading and writing for the SIM music stack.

This crate parses the on-disk `.mid`/`.smf` byte format into the in-memory
[ SmfFile](https://docs.rs/struct.SmfFile.html) model and serialises it back, reusing the event types from

[. It covers the three SMF formats (](https://docs.rs/sim-lib-midi-core/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_lib_midi_core/index.html)

`sim_lib_midi_core`[), the variable-length quantity encoding (](https://docs.rs/enum.SmfFormat.html)

`SmfFormat`[/](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_vlq.html)

`encode_vlq`[), running status, and track canonicalisation/merging. Reading is](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_vlq.html)

`decode_vlq`[; writing is](https://docs.rs/fn.read_smf.html)

`read_smf`[(or](https://docs.rs/fn.write_smf.html)

`write_smf`[for running-status control). Only metric (ticks-per-quarter) division is supported; SMPTE division is rejected.](https://docs.rs/fn.write_smf_with_options.html)

`write_smf_with_options`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Round-tripping a minimal single-track file:

```
use sim_lib_midi_smf::{read_smf, write_smf, SmfFile, SmfFormat, SmfTrack};
use sim_lib_midi_core::{
    MetaEvent, MidiEvent, MidiPayload, TickTime, synthetic_origin,
};
let file = SmfFile {
    format: SmfFormat::SingleTrack,
    tpq: 480,
    tracks: vec![SmfTrack {
        events: vec![MidiEvent {
            time: TickTime::new(0, 480).unwrap(),
            origin: synthetic_origin(),
            payload: MidiPayload::Meta(MetaEvent::EndOfTrack),
        }],
    }],
};
let bytes = write_smf(&file).unwrap();
let parsed = read_smf(&bytes).unwrap();
assert_eq!(parsed.format, SmfFormat::SingleTrack);
assert_eq!(parsed.tpq, 480);
```
The variable-length quantity codec is reversible:

```
use std::io::Cursor;
use sim_lib_midi_smf::{decode_vlq, encode_vlq};
let bytes = encode_vlq(0x4000);
assert_eq!(decode_vlq(&mut Cursor::new(bytes)).unwrap(), 0x4000);
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [SmfFile](https://docs.rs/struct.SmfFile.html)
- A parsed Standard MIDI File: its format, resolution, and tracks.
- [SmfMerge](https://docs.rs/struct.SmfMergeCursor.html)- Cursor
- An iterator that merges all tracks of an `SmfFile`
- [SmfTrack](https://docs.rs/struct.SmfTrack.html)
- One track: an ordered list of timestamped events.
- [SmfWrite](https://docs.rs/struct.SmfWriteOptions.html)- Options
- Options controlling SMF serialisation.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [SmfError](https://docs.rs/enum.SmfError.html)
- Errors raised while reading or writing a Standard MIDI File.
- [SmfFormat](https://docs.rs/enum.SmfFormat.html)
- The SMF header format field: how the file’s tracks relate.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_vlq.html)- vlq
- Decodes a MIDI variable-length quantity from `reader`.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_vlq.html)- vlq
- Encodes `value`as a MIDI variable-length quantity (big-endian, 7 bits per byte with the high bit marking continuation).
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_smf.html)- smf
- Parses a complete Standard MIDI File from `bytes`into an`SmfFile`
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_smf.html)- smf
- Serialises `file`to SMF bytes using default options.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_smf_with_options.html)- smf_ - with_ - options
- Serialises `file`to SMF bytes under the given`SmfWriteOptions`

# sim_lib_music_analysis - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-music-analysis/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Analysis of musical material for the SIM music libraries.

This crate derives structural views over music objects. [ DiffRoll](https://docs.rs/struct.DiffRoll.html) turns a

`sim_lib_music_core::PianoRoll` into per-event frames of sounding, starting,
ending, and slurred pitches, and [segments that timeline into chord-bearing intervals with pitch-range, pitch-class, and bit-chord masks. With the](https://docs.rs/struct.ChordWindow.html)

`ChordWindow``discrete-fwht` feature, the `walsh` module adds Walsh-Hadamard
spectral analysis of melodies, contours, and pitch-class windows.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Chord](https://docs.rs/struct.ChordWindow.html)- Window
- A time interval treated as a single chord, with derived pitch masks.
- [Diff](https://docs.rs/struct.DiffFrame.html)- Frame
- Snapshot of pitch activity at one instant of a `DiffRoll`
- [Diff](https://docs.rs/struct.DiffRoll.html)- Roll
- Event-aligned view of a piano roll as a sequence of difference frames.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Chord](https://docs.rs/enum.ChordWindowMode.html)- Window - Mode
- Selects which pitches a chord window draws from each frame.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [chord_](https://docs.rs/fn.chord_windows_from_diff_roll.html)- windows_ - from_ - diff_ - roll
- Computes chord windows from an existing difference roll under the given mode.
- [chord_](https://docs.rs/fn.chord_windows_from_piano_roll.html)- windows_ - from_ - piano_ - roll
- Computes chord windows directly from a piano roll under the given mode.

# sim_lib_music_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-music-core/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Core music model layer for the SIM music constellation.

SIM is a Rust runtime with multiple codec surfaces; this crate supplies the concrete music domain that those surfaces operate on. It defines the music object model (notes, chords, melodies, scores), the descriptor metadata that describes music components and their ports and parameters, events and lanes, the piano roll and time grid, players and playables, performances and takes, the arranger, freeze surfaces, traces, the component registry, and the citizen integration that registers these types with the runtime.

- Single placement of playable material at a point on the arranger timeline.

- A position or duration in MIDI-style ticks, re-exporting `TickTime`.
- [Time](https://docs.rs/type.Time.html)
- Exact musical time measured in whole notes as a rational number of beats.

# sim_lib_pitch_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-pitch-core/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Core pitch theory primitives for the SIM music libraries.

This crate defines the foundational pitch types shared across the `sim-lib-pitch-*`
constellation: the mod-12 [ PitchClass](https://docs.rs/struct.PitchClass.html), the octave-aware

[, the letter-plus-accidental](https://docs.rs/struct.Pitch.html)

`Pitch`[, and the](https://docs.rs/struct.SpelledPitch.html)

`SpelledPitch`[measured in semitones. Higher-level crates (sets, scales, chords, namers) build on these primitives rather than redefining their own pitch representations.](https://docs.rs/struct.Interval.html)

`Interval`Pitch classes use the twelve-tone equal-tempered convention where `C = 0` and
values increase by semitone up to `B = 11`. Octave-aware pitches use the MIDI
convention in which middle C (`C4`) is MIDI note 60.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Interval](https://docs.rs/struct.Interval.html)
- A pitch interval measured in semitones.
- [Pitch](https://docs.rs/struct.Pitch.html)
- An octave-aware pitch: a `PitchClass`
- [Pitch](https://docs.rs/struct.PitchClass.html)- Class
- A mod-12 pitch class, where `C = 0`and values increase by semitone to`B = 11`.
- [Spelled](https://docs.rs/struct.SpelledPitch.html)- Pitch
- A spelled pitch: a diatonic `Letter`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Letter](https://docs.rs/enum.Letter.html)
- A diatonic letter name, independent of accidental.
- [Pitch](https://docs.rs/enum.PitchError.html)- Error
- Error returned when a pitch, pitch class, or interval cannot be constructed or parsed.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_interval.html)- interval
- Parses one of the recognized interval tokens (`"P5"`,`"m3"`,`"M7"`,`"TT"`) into an`Interval`
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_pitch.html)- pitch
- Parses a pitch spelling such as `"C4"`,`"Eb5"`, or`"Cs4"`into a`Pitch`

# sim_lib_pitch_namer - Rust

## Expand description

Multi-school cluster naming for the SIM music libraries.

`NamingSchool`[. The registry can label a pitch-class set in every school at once and translate a label from one school to another. The schools themselves live in the](https://docs.rs/struct.NamerRegistry.html)

`NamerRegistry``sim-lib-pitch-namer-*` sibling crates; this
crate composes them and exposes them as a SIM runtime library through

# thiserror - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thiserror/^1/

## Expand description

This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library’s
[ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/error/trait.Error.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DataStoreError {
    #[error("data store disconnected")]
    Disconnect(#[from] io::Error),
    #[error("the data for key `{0}` is not available")]
    Redaction(String),
    #[error("invalid header (expected {expected:?}, found {found:?})")]
    InvalidHeader {
        expected: String,
        found: String,
    },
    #[error("unknown data store error")]
    Unknown,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Thiserror deliberately does not appear in your public API. You get the same thing as if you had written an implementation of `std::error::Error`by hand, and switching from handwritten impls to thiserror or vice versa is not a breaking change.
-
Errors may be enums, structs with named fields, tuple structs, or unit structs.
-
A `Display`impl is generated for your error if you provide`#[error("...")]`messages on the struct or each variant of your enum, as shown above in the example.The messages support a shorthand for interpolating fields from the error. - `#[error("{var}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.0)`
- `#[error("{var:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.0)`
 These shorthands can be used together with any additional format args, which may be arbitrary expressions. For example: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("invalid rdo_lookahead_frames {0} (expected < {})", i32::MAX)] InvalidLookahead(u32), }`If one of the additional expression arguments needs to refer to a field of the struct or enum, then refer to named fields as `.var`and tuple fields as`.0`.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("first letter must be lowercase but was {:?}", first_char(.0))] WrongCase(String), #[error("invalid index {idx}, expected at least {} and at most {}", .limits.lo, .limits.hi)] OutOfBounds { idx: usize, limits: Limits }, }`
-
A `From`impl is generated for each variant that contains a`#[from]`attribute.The variant using `#[from]`must not contain any other fields beyond the source error (and possibly a backtrace — see below). Usually`#[from]`fields are unnamed, but`#[from]`is allowed on a named field too.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io(#[from] io::Error), Glob(#[from] globset::Error), }`
-
The Error trait’s `source()`method is implemented to return whichever field has a`#[source]`attribute or is named`source`, if any. This is for identifying the underlying lower level error that caused your error.The `#[from]`attribute always implies that the same field is`#[source]`, so you don’t ever need to specify both attributes.Any error type that implements `std::error::Error`or dereferences to`dyn std::error::Error`will work as a source.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, #[source] // optional if field name is `source` source: anyhow::Error, }`
-
The Error trait’s `provide()`method is implemented to provide whichever field has a type named`Backtrace`, if any, as a`std::backtrace::Backtrace`. Using`Backtrace`in errors requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`use std::backtrace::Backtrace; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, backtrace: Backtrace, // automatically detected }`
-
If a field is both a source (named `source`, or has`#[source]`or`#[from]`attribute)*and*is marked`#[backtrace]`, then the Error trait’s`provide()`method is forwarded to the source’s`provide`so that both layers of the error share the same backtrace. The`#[backtrace]`attribute requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[backtrace] source: io::Error, }, }`
-
For variants that use `#[from]`and also contain a`Backtrace`field, a backtrace is captured from within the`From`impl.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[from] source: io::Error, backtrace: Backtrace, }, }`
-
Errors may use `error(transparent)`to forward the source and Display methods straight through to an underlying error without adding an additional message. This would be appropriate for enums that need an “anything else” variant.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { ... #[error(transparent)] Other(#[from] anyhow::Error), // source and Display delegate to anyhow::Error }`Another use case is hiding implementation details of an error representation behind an opaque error type, so that the representation is able to evolve without breaking the crate’s public API. `// PublicError is public, but opaque and easy to keep compatible. #[derive(Error, Debug)] #[error(transparent)] pub struct PublicError(#[from] ErrorRepr); impl PublicError { // Accessors for anything we do want to expose publicly. } // Private and free to change across minor version of the crate. #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum ErrorRepr { ... }`
-
See also the `anyhow`

---

# sim_lib_music_lower - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-music-lower/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Lowers music from higher-level representations to renderable ones.

Lowering is the inverse of lifting: it takes a structured music object or
[ Score](https://docs.rs/sim-lib-music-core/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_lib_music_core/model/struct.Score.html) and renders it down to a concrete,
playable Standard MIDI File.

[and](https://docs.rs/fn.lower.html)

`lower`[produce an in-memory](https://docs.rs/fn.lower_score.html)

`lower_score``SmfFile`, while [serializes that file to bytes.](https://docs.rs/fn.write_smf.html)

`write_smf`[controls ticks-per-quarter resolution, the tempo map, and how voices are split across MIDI tracks.](https://docs.rs/struct.LowerOpts.html)

`LowerOpts`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Lower](https://docs.rs/struct.LowerOpts.html)- Opts
- Options controlling how music is lowered to a MIDI file.
- [Tempo](https://docs.rs/struct.TempoMap.html)- Map
- A piecewise-constant tempo curve mapping music time to beats per minute.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Lower](https://docs.rs/enum.LowerError.html)- Error
- Error raised while lowering music to a MIDI file.
- [Track](https://docs.rs/enum.TrackSplit.html)- Split
- Policy for distributing lowered notes across MIDI tracks.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [default_](https://docs.rs/fn.default_us_per_quarter.html)- us_ - per_ - quarter
- Returns the default microseconds-per-quarter-note tempo value.
- [equivalent_](https://docs.rs/fn.equivalent_under_lowering.html)- under_ - lowering
- Returns whether two music objects lower to byte-identical MIDI files.
- [lower](https://docs.rs/fn.lower.html)
- Lowers any music object into an in-memory MIDI file.
- [lower_](https://docs.rs/fn.lower_score.html)- score
- Lowers a `Score`into a MIDI file, applying the score’s tempo to the map.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_smf.html)- smf
- Lowers a `Score`and serializes the resulting MIDI file to bytes.

# sim_lib_music_lift - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sim-lib-music-lift/0.1.0-rc.1/target-redirect/sim_lib_music_lift/

## Expand description

Lifts music from lower-level representations to higher-level ones.

A lift raises a concrete, low-level representation (a parsed MIDI/SMF file)
into a richer, more structured music representation: a `PianoRoll`, a
`DiffRoll` analysis view, a chord `Progression`, or a `Counterpoint` of
separated voices. Each lifter implements [ MidiLifter](https://docs.rs/trait.MidiLifter.html) and returns a

[carrying the lifted value alongside diagnostics describing lossy or ambiguous decisions.](https://docs.rs/struct.LiftReport.html)

`LiftReport`The `lift_to_*` free functions are convenience entry points over the
[ MidiToPianoRoll](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToPianoRoll.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToDiffRoll.html)

`MidiToDiffRoll`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToProgression.html)

`MidiToProgression`[lifters, and](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToCounterpoint.html)

`MidiToCounterpoint`[registers them as host-side runtime exports.](https://docs.rs/struct.MusicLiftLib.html)

`MusicLiftLib`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Counterpoint](https://docs.rs/struct.CounterpointLiftOpts.html)- Lift - Opts
- Options controlling the MIDI-to-counterpoint lift.
- [Lift](https://docs.rs/struct.LiftReport.html)- Report
- A lifted value paired with diagnostics describing lossy or ambiguous choices.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToCounterpoint.html)- ToCounterpoint
- Lifter producing a `Counterpoint`of separated voices from a MIDI file.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToDiffRoll.html)- ToDiff - Roll
- Lifter producing a `DiffRoll`note-boundary analysis view from a MIDI file.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToPianoRoll.html)- ToPiano - Roll
- Lifter producing a `PianoRoll`of timed notes from a MIDI file.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToProgression.html)- ToProgression
- Lifter producing a chord `Progression`from a MIDI file.
- [Music](https://docs.rs/struct.MusicLiftLib.html)- Lift - Lib
- Loadable library that registers the MIDI lifters as host-side runtime values.
- [Progression](https://docs.rs/struct.ProgressionLiftOpts.html)- Lift - Opts
- Options controlling the MIDI-to-progression lift.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Label](https://docs.rs/enum.LabelStrategy.html)- Strategy
- Chord-label selection policy for the progression lifter.
- [Lift](https://docs.rs/enum.LiftError.html)- Error
- Error raised while lifting MIDI into a higher-level music representation.
- [Voice](https://docs.rs/enum.VoiceAssignment.html)- Assignment
- Voice-splitting policy for the counterpoint lifter.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Midi](https://docs.rs/trait.MidiLifter.html)- Lifter
- A lifter that raises a parsed MIDI file into a higher-level music value.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_music_lift_lib.html)- music_ - lift_ - lib
- Loads `MusicLiftLib``cx`once, recording lifter export records.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_counterpoint.html)- to_ - counterpoint
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `Counterpoint`, discarding diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_counterpoint_report.html)- to_ - counterpoint_ - report
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `Counterpoint`with diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_diff_roll.html)- to_ - diff_ - roll
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `DiffRoll`, discarding diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_diff_roll_report.html)- to_ - diff_ - roll_ - report
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `DiffRoll`with diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_piano_roll.html)- to_ - piano_ - roll
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `PianoRoll`, discarding diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_piano_roll_report.html)- to_ - piano_ - roll_ - report
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `PianoRoll`with diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_progression.html)- to_ - progression
- Lifts a MIDI file to a chord `Progression`, discarding diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_progression_report.html)- to_ - progression_ - report
- Lifts a MIDI file to a chord `Progression`with diagnostics.

- A lifted value paired with diagnostics describing lossy or ambiguous choices.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToCounterpoint.html)- ToCounterpoint
- Lifter producing a `Counterpoint`of separated voices from a MIDI file.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToDiffRoll.html)- ToDiff - Roll
- Lifter producing a `DiffRoll`note-boundary analysis view from a MIDI file.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToPianoRoll.html)- ToPiano - Roll
- Lifter producing a `PianoRoll`of timed notes from a MIDI file.
- [Midi](https://docs.rs/struct.MidiToProgression.html)- ToProgression
- Lifter producing a chord `Progression`from a MIDI file.
- [Music](https://docs.rs/struct.MusicLiftLib.html)- Lift - Lib
- Loadable library that registers the MIDI lifters as host-side runtime values.
- [Progression](https://docs.rs/struct.ProgressionLiftOpts.html)- Lift - Opts
- Options controlling the MIDI-to-progression lift.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Label](https://docs.rs/enum.LabelStrategy.html)- Strategy
- Chord-label selection policy for the progression lifter.
- [Lift](https://docs.rs/enum.LiftError.html)- Error
- Error raised while lifting MIDI into a higher-level music representation.
- [Voice](https://docs.rs/enum.VoiceAssignment.html)- Assignment
- Voice-splitting policy for the counterpoint lifter.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Midi](https://docs.rs/trait.MidiLifter.html)- Lifter
- A lifter that raises a parsed MIDI file into a higher-level music value.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_music_lift_lib.html)- music_ - lift_ - lib
- Loads `MusicLiftLib``cx`once, recording lifter export records.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_counterpoint.html)- to_ - counterpoint
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `Counterpoint`, discarding diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_counterpoint_report.html)- to_ - counterpoint_ - report
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `Counterpoint`with diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_diff_roll.html)- to_ - diff_ - roll
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `DiffRoll`, discarding diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_diff_roll_report.html)- to_ - diff_ - roll_ - report
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `DiffRoll`with diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_piano_roll.html)- to_ - piano_ - roll
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `PianoRoll`, discarding diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_piano_roll_report.html)- to_ - piano_ - roll_ - report
- Lifts a MIDI file to a `PianoRoll`with diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_progression.html)- to_ - progression
- Lifts a MIDI file to a chord `Progression`, discarding diagnostics.
- [lift_](https://docs.rs/fn.lift_to_progression_report.html)- to_ - progression_ - report
- Lifts a MIDI file to a chord `Progression`with diagnostics.

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-music-lift/0.1.0-rc.1/src/sim_lib_music_lift/lib.rs.html

# sim_lib_music_lift/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Lifts music from lower-level representations to higher-level ones.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! A lift raises a concrete, low-level representation (a parsed MIDI/SMF file)
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! into a richer, more structured music representation: a `PianoRoll`, a
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! `DiffRoll` analysis view, a chord `Progression`, or a `Counterpoint` of
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! separated voices. Each lifter implements [`MidiLifter`] and returns a
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! [`LiftReport`] carrying the lifted value alongside diagnostics describing
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! lossy or ambiguous decisions.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! The `lift_to_*` free functions are convenience entry points over the
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! [`MidiToPianoRoll`], [`MidiToDiffRoll`], [`MidiToProgression`], and
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! [`MidiToCounterpoint`] lifters, and [`MusicLiftLib`] registers them as
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! host-side runtime exports.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
[15](https://docs.rs#15)#![deny(missing_docs)]
[16](https://docs.rs#16)
[17](https://docs.rs#17)mod collect;
[18](https://docs.rs#18)mod counterpoint;
[19](https://docs.rs#19)mod model;
[20](https://docs.rs#20)mod progression;
[21](https://docs.rs#21)mod runtime;
[22](https://docs.rs#22)
[23](https://docs.rs#23)pub use model::*;
[24](https://docs.rs#24)pub use runtime::{MusicLiftLib, install_music_lift_lib};
[25](https://docs.rs#25)
[26](https://docs.rs#26)#[cfg(test)]
[27](https://docs.rs#27)mod tests;

---

`pub struct MusicLiftLib;`## Expand description

Loadable library that registers the MIDI lifters as host-side runtime values.

It exports one value per lifter symbol plus a `MidiLifterRegistry` table that
enumerates them with their layer, shape, and capability metadata.

## Expand description

The minimum-notes-per-chord threshold was not positive.

The per-track voice cap was not positive.

A construction error surfaced from `sim-lib-music-core`.

## Expand description

Voice-splitting policy for the counterpoint lifter.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

### ChannelOnly

Separate voices by MIDI channel only.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TrackThenChannel)

### TrackThenChannel

### HighestFirst

Assign overlapping notes highest pitch first.

### LowestFirst

# uuid - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uuid/^1.8/

## Expand description

Generate and parse universally unique identifiers (UUIDs).

Here’s an example of a UUID:

`67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c8`A UUID is a unique 128-bit value, stored as 16 octets, and regularly formatted as a hex string in five groups. UUIDs are used to assign unique identifiers to entities without requiring a central allocating authority.

They are particularly useful in distributed systems, though can be used in disparate areas, such as databases and network protocols. Typically a UUID is displayed in a readable string form as a sequence of hexadecimal digits, separated into groups by hyphens.

The uniqueness property is not strictly guaranteed, however for all practical purposes, it can be assumed that an unintentional collision would be extremely unlikely.

UUIDs have a number of standardized encodings that are specified in [RFC 9562](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc9562.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
# Lets you generate random UUIDs
features = [
    "v4",
]
```
When you want a UUID, you can generate one:

```
use uuid::Uuid;
let id = Uuid::new_v4();
```
If you have a UUID value, you can use its string literal form inline:

```
use uuid::{uuid, Uuid};
const ID: Uuid = uuid!("67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c8");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#working-with-different-uuid-versions)Working with different UUID versions

This library supports all standardized methods for generating UUIDs through individual Cargo features.

By default, this crate depends on nothing but the Rust standard library and can parse and format UUIDs, but cannot generate them. Depending on the kind of UUID you’d like to work with, there are Cargo features that enable generating them:

- `v1`- Version 1 UUIDs using a timestamp and monotonic counter.
- `v3`- Version 3 UUIDs based on the MD5 hash of some data.
- `v4`- Version 4 UUIDs with random data.
- `v5`- Version 5 UUIDs based on the SHA1 hash of some data.
- `v6`- Version 6 UUIDs using a timestamp and monotonic counter.
- `v7`- Version 7 UUIDs using a Unix timestamp.
- `v8`- Version 8 UUIDs using user-defined data.

This library also includes a [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html) type that can be used to help construct UUIDs of any
version without any additional dependencies or features. It’s a lower-level API than

[that can be used when you need control over implicit requirements on things like a source of randomness.](https://docs.rs/struct.Uuid.html)

`Uuid`[§](https://docs.rs#which-uuid-version-should-i-use)Which UUID version should I use?

If you just want to generate unique identifiers then consider version 4 (`v4`) UUIDs. If you want
to use UUIDs as database keys or need to sort them then consider version 7 (`v7`) UUIDs.
Other versions should generally be avoided unless there’s an existing need for them.

Some UUID versions supersede others. Prefer version 6 over version 1 and version 5 over version 3.

[§](https://docs.rs#other-features)Other features

Other crate features can also be useful beyond the version support:

- `serde`- adds the ability to serialize and deserialize a UUID using- `serde`.
- `borsh`- adds the ability to serialize and deserialize a UUID using- `borsh`.
- `arbitrary`- adds an- `Arbitrary`trait implementation to- `Uuid`for fuzzing.
- `fast-rng`- uses a faster algorithm for generating random UUIDs when available. This feature requires more dependencies to compile, but is just as suitable for UUIDs as the default algorithm.
- `rng-rand`- forces- `rand`as the backend for randomness.
- `rng-getrandom`- forces- `getrandom`as the backend for randomness.
- `bytemuck`- adds a- `Pod`trait implementation to- `Uuid`for byte manipulation

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

Some features are unstable. They may be incomplete or depend on other unstable libraries. These include:

- `zerocopy`- adds support for zero-copy deserialization using the- `zerocopy`library.

Unstable features may break between minor releases.

To allow unstable features, you’ll need to enable the Cargo feature as
normal, but also pass an additional flag through your environment to opt-in
to unstable `uuid` features:

`RUSTFLAGS="--cfg uuid_unstable"`[§](https://docs.rs#building-for-other-targets)Building for other targets

[§](https://docs.rs#webassembly)WebAssembly

For WebAssembly, enable the `js` feature:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
features = [
    "v4",
    "v7",
    "js",
]
```
[§](https://docs.rs#embedded)Embedded

For embedded targets without the standard library, you’ll need to
disable default features when building `uuid`:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
default-features = false
```
Some additional features are supported in no-std environments:

- `v1`,- `v3`,- `v5`,- `v6`, and- `v8`.
- `serde`.

If you need to use `v4` or `v7` in a no-std environment, you’ll need to
produce random bytes yourself and then pass them to [ Builder::from_random_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html#method.from_random_bytes)
without enabling the

`v4` or `v7` features.If you’re using `getrandom`, you can specify the `rng-getrandom` or `rng-rand`
features of `uuid` and configure `getrandom`’s provider per its docs. `uuid`
may upgrade its version of `getrandom` in minor releases.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Parse a UUID given in the simple format and print it as a URN:

```
let my_uuid = Uuid::parse_str("a1a2a3a4b1b2c1c2d1d2d3d4d5d6d7d8")?;
println!("{}", my_uuid.urn());
```
Generate a random UUID and print it out in hexadecimal form:

```
// Note that this requires the `v4` feature to be enabled.
let my_uuid = Uuid::new_v4();
println!("{}", my_uuid);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#references)References

# sourceatlas 0.2.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sourceatlas/latest

# SourceAtlas

SourceAtlas is a command-line tool written in Rust that scans a source code repository and generates useful statistics.

I started this project as a way to learn Rust by building something practical instead of only completing exercises. The goal isn't to compete with existing tools, but to build a clean, well-structured application while learning more about idiomatic Rust and software engineering.

## Features

Current features include:

- Recursive directory scanning
- Ignores common build and IDE directories:
- `target`
- `build`
- `node_modules`
- `.idea`
- `.vscode`

- Reports:
- Directories scanned
- Files scanned
- Files analyzed
- Files skipped
- Total lines

- Gracefully skips unreadable or binary files
- Unit tested

## Installation

Install from crates.io:

```
```
Or build from source:

```
```
## Usage

Scan the current directory:

```
```
Scan another directory:

```
```
## Example Output

```
-------------
|SourceAtlas|
-------------
Scanning Git repo
LANGUAGE STATS
Rust: 100.0%
DIRECTORIES
--------
total directories: 4
TOTALS
--------
total files found: 13
total files analyzed: 7
total files skipped: 6
total lines: 425
```
*The above output is generated when running SourceAtlas on itself*

## Roadmap

Some features I'd like to add:

- More visually appealing report generation
- Custom ignore files
- JSON output
- Markdown reports

## License

This project is licensed under the MIT License.

# sourceatlas 0.2.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sourceatlas/0.2.3/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# tempfile 3.27.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/tempfile/^3.27.0

# tempfile

A secure, cross-platform, temporary file library for Rust. In addition to creating temporary files, this library also allows users to securely open multiple independent references to the same temporary file (useful for consumer/producer patterns and surprisingly difficult to implement securely).

## Usage

Minimum required Rust version: 1.63.0

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "3"
```
## Supported Platforms

This crate supports all major operating systems:

- Linux
- Android
- MacOS
- Windows
- FreeBSD (likely other BSDs but we don't have CI for them)
- RedoxOS
- Wasm (build and link only, Wasm doesn't have a filesystem)
- WASI P1 & P2.

However:

- Android, RedoxOS, Wasm, and WASI targets all require the latest stable rust compiler.
- WASI P1/P2 does not define a default temporary directory. You'll need to explicitly call `tempfile::env::override_temp_dir`with a valid directory or temporary file creation will panic on this platform.
- WASI P1/P2 does not have file permissions.
- You *may*need to override the temporary directory in Android as well to point at your application's per-app cache directory.

## Example

```
use File;
use ;
```

# sourceatlas 0.1.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sourceatlas/0.1.1

# SourceAtlas

SourceAtlas is a command-line tool written in Rust that scans a source code repository and generates useful statistics.

I started this project as a way to learn Rust by building something practical instead of only completing exercises. The goal isn't to compete with existing tools, but to build a clean, well-structured application while learning more about idiomatic Rust and software engineering.

## Features

Current features include:

- Recursive directory scanning
- Ignores common build and IDE directories:
- `target`
- `build`
- `node_modules`
- `.idea`
- `.vscode`

- Reports:
- Directories scanned
- Files scanned
- Files analyzed
- Files skipped
- Total lines
- Blank lines
- Non-blank lines
- Characters
- Functions (currently Rust only)
- TODO comments

- Gracefully skips unreadable or binary files
- Unit tested

## Installation

Install from crates.io:

```
```
Or build from source:

```
```
## Usage

Scan the current directory:

```
```
Scan another directory:

```
```
## Example Output

```
----------
|sourceatlas|
----------
DIRECTORIES
--------
total directories: 55
FILES
--------
total files found: 86
total files analyzed: 43
total files skipped: 43
total lines: 1607
total characters: 40438
total non-blank lines: 1372
total blank lines: 235
total functions: 16
total TODO's: 26
```
*The above output is generated when running sourceatlas on itself*

## Roadmap

Some features I'd like to add:

- More visually appealing report generation
- Support for more languages
- Custom ignore files
- JSON output
- Markdown reports
- Better language detection
- Parallel directory scanning
- Additional repository metrics

## Why SourceAtlas?

The idea behind the name is simple: rather than just counting lines of code, SourceAtlas aims to provide an overview of a source tree—almost like a map of a repository.

# sidereon 0.11.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sidereon/0.11.0

# sidereon

GNSS and astrodynamics for Rust: propagate satellites, predict passes, solve precise positions (SPP / RTK / PPP), and convert between coordinate frames and time scales, checked against the references the field trusts (Vallado, Skyfield, IGS, IERS).

It's a pure-Rust engine, fast and `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at the surface, with
one ergonomic crate that re-exports the whole stack. You just `cargo add sidereon`.

## Install

```
cargo add sidereon
```
## Quickstart: when does the ISS fly over you?

No data files, no setup: give it a two-line element set and a ground station, and ask when the satellite is above the horizon.

```
use ;
use ;
use Satellite;
```
A typical run prints something like:

```
08:30 UTC |  6.8 min | peak 88 deg
15:01 UTC |  6.6 min | peak 56 deg
16:39 UTC |  3.5 min | peak 14 deg
```
Each [`SatellitePass`] gives you acquisition (`aos`), loss (`los`), culmination
time, and peak elevation. The same `sidereon::passes` module has `look_angle`
(azimuth / elevation / range to a satellite at an instant) and `propagate_teme_arc`
for raw state vectors; `Satellite` from `sidereon::sgp4` is the propagator behind
all of it.

## Precise positioning

The positioning engine is the other half of the library: feed it pseudoranges and a precise-ephemeris (SP3) product and it returns a least-squares fix.

```
use ;
use ;
let sp3 = load_sp3?;
let inputs = SolveInputs ;
let fix = solve_spp?;
println!;    // ItrfPositionM: ECEF metres
println!;    // Some(Wgs84Geodetic): lat / lon / height
println!;   // the satellites that contributed
```
`solve_rtk_float_with`, `solve_rtk_fixed_with`, `solve_ppp_float_with`, and
`solve_ppp_fixed_with` follow the same pattern: a typed config in, a result struct
with ECEF/geodetic position, residuals, DOP, and status out. One [`Error`] enum
unifies every product-parse and solve failure, and `solve_spp_batch` fans a fleet
of epochs across a rayon pool, bit-identical to the serial path.

## What's in the box

- **Orbits:**SGP4/TLE and OMM, numerical propagation with atmospheric drag and decay/reentry prediction, Kepler and anomaly conversions, classical and equinoctial elements, passes, look angles
- **Frames, time & geodesy:**TEME ↔ GCRS ↔ ITRS, GMST/GAST, geodetic ↔ ECEF, UTC/TT/TDB/UT1, EGM96 geoid, DTED terrain elevation
- **Bodies & almanac:**Sun/Moon/planet apparent places (geocentric or topocentric RA/Dec), Sun and Moon rise/set, seasons, moon phases, eclipses, planetary transits, plus JPL SPK (DAF/.bsp) kernels
- **Observation geometry:**angular separation and position angle, phase/beta/parallactic angles, sub-solar and sub-observer points, terminator, satellite visual magnitude
- **Positioning:**SPP, RTK (float/fixed), PPP (float/fixed), DOP, velocity, robust fault detection and exclusion
- **GNSS data:**SP3, RINEX (obs/nav/clock), CRINEX, ANTEX, broadcast ephemeris, Bias-SINEX / CODE DCB biases, source-agnostic ephemeris sampling
- **Corrections:**SBAS, RTCM SSR and Galileo HAS orbit/clock/bias correction stores
- **Space situational awareness:**conjunction/TCA screening, collision probability, CDM, covariance, relative motion (RIC/RTN/LVLH, Clohessy-Wiltshire)
- **RF:**link budget (FSPL, EIRP, C/N0, antenna gain)

The product parsers, look-angle helpers, and propagation shortcuts live at the
crate root (`load_sp3`, `solve_spp`, `passes`, `sgp4`, `tle`, `tca`, `relative`,
`almanac`); the full astrodynamics tree is under `sidereon::astro`. Lower-level RTK/PPP internals stay
behind the explicit `sidereon::raw` escape hatch so the ergonomic surface stays
small.

## Other languages

sidereon is one validated engine with first-class interfaces in **Rust**,
**Python**, **C**, **Elixir**, and **WebAssembly**: same numbers everywhere.
See the live demo and docs at [sidereon.dev](https://sidereon.dev).

## How it's validated

The SGP4 propagator is a Rust port of David Vallado's reference implementation, bit-exact to it. Frames and time are checked against Skyfield and IERS; the positioning stack is checked against IGS products.

MIT licensed. The engine's SGP4 propagation credits David Vallado (AIAA 2006);
see the `sidereon-core` crate for full attribution.

---

# flate2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/flate2/^1/

## Expand description

A DEFLATE-based stream compression/decompression library

This library provides support for compression and decompression of DEFLATE-based streams:

- the DEFLATE format itself
- the zlib format
- gzip

These three formats are all closely related and largely only differ in their headers/footers. This crate has three types in each submodule for dealing with these three formats.

[§](https://docs.rs#implementation)Implementation

In addition to supporting three formats, this crate supports several different
backends, controlled through this crate’s *features flags*:

-
`default`, or`rust_backend`- this implementation currently uses the`miniz_oxide`crate which is a port of`miniz.c`to Rust. This feature does not require a C compiler, and only uses safe Rust code.Note that the `rust_backend`feature may at some point be switched to use`zlib-rs`, and that`miniz_oxide`should be used explicitly if this is not desired.
-
`zlib-rs`- this implementation utilizes the`zlib-rs`crate, a Rust rewrite of zlib. This backend is the fastest, at the cost of some`unsafe`Rust code.

Several backends implemented in C are also available. These are useful in case you are already using a specific C implementation and need the result of compression to be bit-identical. See the crate’s README for details on the available C backends.

The `zlib-rs` backend typically outperforms all the C implementations.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `miniz_oxide`- *(enabled by default)*— This implementation uses only safe Rust code and doesn’t require a C compiler. It provides good performance for most use cases while being completely portable.
- `default`

[§](https://docs.rs#user-facing-backend-features)User-Facing Backend Features

Choose one of these features to select the compression backend.
Only one backend should be enabled at a time, or else one will see an unstable order which is currently
`zlib-ng`, `zlib-rs`, `cloudflare_zlib`, `miniz_oxide` and which may change at any time.

-
`rust_backend`*(enabled by default)*— Use the pure Rust`miniz_oxide`backend (default). This implementation uses only safe Rust code and doesn’t require a C compiler. It provides good performance for most use cases while being completely portable.Note that this feature at some point may be switched to use `zlib-rs`instead.
-
`zlib-rs``unsafe`code. It does not require a C compiler but uses`unsafe`Rust for optimization.
-
`miniz_oxide`*(enabled by default)*— Use the pure Rust`miniz_oxide`backend.
-
`zlib`
-
`zlib-default``zlib`but enables additional features from libz-sys.
-
`zlib-ng-compat``zlib-ng`feature. When using this feature, if any crate in your dependency graph explicitly requests stock zlib, or uses libz-sys directly without`default-features = false`, you’ll get stock zlib rather than zlib-ng. See[the libz-sys README](https://github.com/rust-lang/libz-sys/blob/main/README.md)for details. To avoid that, use the`"zlib-ng"`feature instead.
-
`zlib-ng`
-
`cloudflare_zlib`- ⚠ Does not support 32-bit CPUs and is incompatible with mingw.
- ⚠ May cause conflicts if other crates use different zlib versions.

-
`miniz-sys``rust_backend`, provided for backwards compatibility. Use`rust_backend`instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#internal-features)Internal Features

These features are used internally for backend selection and should not be enabled directly by users. They are documented here to aid with maintenance.

- `any_zlib`- **Internal:**Marker feature indicating that any zlib-based C backend is enabled. This is automatically enabled by- `zlib-rs`,- `zlib`,- `zlib-ng`,- `zlib-ng-compat`, and- `cloudflare_zlib`. Do not enable this feature directly; instead, choose a specific backend feature.
- `any_c_zlib`- **Internal:**Marker feature indicating that any C based fully zlib compatible backend is enabled. This is automatically enabled by- `zlib`,- `zlib-ng`,- `zlib-ng-compat`, and- `cloudflare_zlib`. Do not enable this feature directly; instead, choose a specific backend feature.
- `any_impl`- *(enabled by default)*—- **Internal:**Marker feature indicating that any compression backend is enabled. This is automatically enabled by all backend features to ensure at least one implementation is available. Do not enable this feature directly; instead, choose a specific backend feature.

[§](https://docs.rs#ambiguous-feature-selection)Ambiguous feature selection

As Cargo features are additive, while backends are not, there is an order in which backends become active if multiple are selected.

- zlib-ng
- zlib-rs
- cloudflare_zlib
- miniz_oxide

[§](https://docs.rs#organization)Organization

This crate consists of three main modules: `bufread`, `read`, and `write`. Each module
implements DEFLATE, zlib, and gzip for [ std::io::BufRead](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.BufRead.html) input types,

[input types, and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)

`std::io::Read`[output types respectively.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html)

`std::io::Write`Use the [ bufread](https://docs.rs/bufread/index.html) implementations if you can provide a

`BufRead` type for the input.
The `&[u8]` slice type implements the `BufRead` trait.The [ read](https://docs.rs/read/index.html) implementations conveniently wrap a

`Read` type in a `BufRead` implementation.
However, the `read` implementations may
[read past the end of the input data](https://github.com/rust-lang/flate2-rs/issues/338), making the

`Read` type useless for subsequent reads of the input. If you need to re-use the
`Read` type, wrap it in a [, use the](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/buffered/bufreader/struct.BufReader.html)

`std::io::BufReader``bufread` implementations,
and perform subsequent reads on the `BufReader`.The [ write](https://docs.rs/write/index.html) implementations are most useful when there is no way to create a

`BufRead`
type, notably when reading async iterators (streams).```
use futures::{Stream, StreamExt};
use std::io::{Result, Write as _};
async fn decompress_gzip_stream<S, I>(stream: S) -> Result<Vec<u8>>
where
    S: Stream<Item = I>,
    I: AsRef<[u8]>
{
    let mut stream = std::pin::pin!(stream);
    let mut w = Vec::<u8>::new();
    let mut decoder = flate2::write::GzDecoder::new(w);
    while let Some(input) = stream.next().await {
        decoder.write_all(input.as_ref())?;
    }
    decoder.finish()
}
```
Note that types which operate over a specific trait often implement the mirroring trait as well.
For example a `bufread::DeflateDecoder<T>` *also* implements the
[ Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html) trait if

`T: Write`. That is, the “dual trait” is forwarded directly
to the underlying object if available.[§](https://docs.rs#about-multi-member-gzip-files)About multi-member Gzip files

While most `gzip` files one encounters will have a single *member* that can be read
with the [ GzDecoder](https://docs.rs/bufread/struct.GzDecoder.html), there may be some files which have multiple members.

A [ GzDecoder](https://docs.rs/bufread/struct.GzDecoder.html) will only read the first member of gzip data, which may unexpectedly
provide partial results when a multi-member gzip file is encountered.

`GzDecoder` is appropriate
for data that is designed to be read as single members from a multi-member file. `bufread::GzDecoder`
and `write::GzDecoder` also allow non-gzip data following gzip data to be handled.The [ MultiGzDecoder](https://docs.rs/bufread/struct.MultiGzDecoder.html) on the other hand will decode all members of a

`gzip` file
into one consecutive stream of bytes, which hides the underlying *members*entirely. If a file contains non-gzip data after the gzip data, MultiGzDecoder will emit an error after decoding the gzip data. This behavior matches the

`gzip`,
`gunzip`, and `zcat` command line tools.## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [bufread](https://docs.rs/bufread/index.html)
- Types which operate over `BufRead`
- [read](https://docs.rs/read/index.html)
- Types which operate over `Read`
- [write](https://docs.rs/write/index.html)
- Types which operate over `Write`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Compress](https://docs.rs/struct.Compress.html)
- Raw in-memory compression stream for blocks of data.
- [Compress](https://docs.rs/struct.CompressError.html)- Error
- Error returned when a compression object is used incorrectly or otherwise generates an error.
- [Compression](https://docs.rs/struct.Compression.html)
- When compressing data, the compression level can be specified by a value in this struct.
- [Crc](https://docs.rs/struct.Crc.html)- `zlib-rs`
- The CRC calculated by a `CrcReader`
- [CrcReader](https://docs.rs/struct.CrcReader.html)
- A wrapper around a `Read`
- [CrcWriter](https://docs.rs/struct.CrcWriter.html)
- A wrapper around a `Write`
- [Decompress](https://docs.rs/struct.Decompress.html)
- Raw in-memory decompression stream for blocks of data.
- [Decompress](https://docs.rs/struct.DecompressError.html)- Error
- Error returned when a decompression object finds that the input stream of bytes was not a valid input stream of bytes.
- [GzBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.GzBuilder.html)

# sidereon_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sidereon-core/^0.11.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#sidereon-core)sidereon-core

The complete Sidereon engine in one crate. It folds the numerical astrodynamics core (orbit propagation, force models, frames, time, SGP4) together with the GNSS domain layer (SP3, broadcast ephemeris, multi-GNSS positioning, RTK/PPP, ionosphere/troposphere, DOP).

- The propagation/astro layer is always present under the `astro`
- The GNSS layer lives behind the default-on `gnss`cargo feature, so a propagation-only consumer can build with`--no-default-features`(plus any astro features it wants) and never compile the IONEX/SP3 parsers.

The GNSS façade is organized by user-facing tasks:

- `ephemeris`
- `rinex`
- `antex`
- `combinations`
- `observables`
- `velocity`
- `positioning`
- `dgnss`
- `quality`
- `observation_qc`
- `signal`
- `ppp_corrections`
- `atmosphere`
- `orbit`

Implementation modules (`sp3`, `rinex_nav`, `spp`, etc.) are crate-private.
This is a clean public surface rather than a compatibility shim around the
original implementation-shaped module layout.

[§](https://docs.rs#units-policy-internal-representation)Units policy (internal representation)

All quantities are stored and computed in **SI base units**, with the frame
and datum encoded in the type name (per the spec’s frames-in-the-type-system
rule), never hidden behind a bare `position_m`:

- **Length / position:**meters (- `_m`). SP3 positions are ITRF/IGS-frame ECEF meters; SPP receiver positions are WGS84/ITRF-compatible ECEF meters. (The- `astro`
- **Time / clock:**seconds (- `_s`). Epochs are represented by the- `astro`- `Instant`/- `TimeScale`), always scale-tagged; there is no bare ambiguous epoch.
- **Velocity:**meters per second (- `_m_s`).
- **Angles:**radians (- `_rad`) internally. Degrees appear only at I/O edges and are named- `_deg`.
- **Frequency:**hertz (- `_hz`).

Field and parameter names carry the unit suffix so the unit is visible at
every call site. Matrix/vector linear algebra uses `nalgebra`
(`DMatrix`/`DVector`) per the spec.
